root_cause.text: The `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function in the MIPI I3C HCI driver lacks synchronization, allowing concurrent invocations from multiple timeout handlers to race when stopping and restarting the DMA ring, causing interleaved ring control operations that corrupt the ring state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `mutex_init(&hci->control_mutex)` in the probe function and wraps the entire `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function body with `guard(mutex)(&hci->control_mutex)`. The CVE description explicitly states that "the function is not serialized and can race with itself" when multiple transfers timeout simultaneously, and that "two instances may interfere with each other - stopping or restarting the ring at unexpected times." The fix serializes access to the critical section where ring control operations (stop, process transfers, restart) occur, preventing concurrent execution of these interdependent operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the control_mutex synchronization primitive during device probe to prevent use of uninitialized mutex.
intent_record.what: Added a single line `mutex_init(&hci->control_mutex);` after the existing `spin_lock_init(&hci->lock);` call in the i3c_hci_probe function.
intent_record.how: This initializes a mutex lock (control_mutex) on the hci device structure during probe time. The mutex will now be properly initialized before any code attempts to acquire it, preventing undefined behavior from using an uninitialized synchronization primitive.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add mutex lock guard to protect DMA dequeue operations from concurrent access and race conditions.
intent_record.what: Added a guard(mutex) macro call for hci->control_mutex at the beginning of the hci_dma_dequeue_xfer function, before the ring control operations.
intent_record.how: This change automatically acquires the control_mutex lock upon function entry and ensures it is released when the function exits (via scope-based lock management). This prevents concurrent access to the ring control register operations and related state, eliminating potential race conditions where multiple threads could simultaneously manipulate the DMA ring state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a control mutex to the i3c_hci structure to protect critical control operations with sleeping-compatible synchronization.
intent_record.what: Added a new field `struct mutex control_mutex;` to the `i3c_hci` structure after the existing `spinlock_t lock;` field.
intent_record.how: This introduces a mutex lock mechanism to the i3c_hci device structure, enabling mutual exclusion for control operations. The mutex can be used to protect critical sections that require exclusive access, complementing the existing spinlock for different synchronization scenarios (mutexes allow sleeping, spinlocks do not).

Author: Nicolas Pitre <npitre@baylibre.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 11 17:05:10 2020 -0500

    i3c/master: introduce the mipi-i3c-hci driver
    
    This adds basic support for hardware implementing the MIPI I3C HCI
    specification. This driver is currently limited by the capabilities
    of the I3C subsystem, meaning things like scheduled commands,
    auto-commands and NCM mode are not yet supported.
    
    This supports version 1.0 of the MIPI I3C
bic_trace_step.reason: The `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function (lines 540-581) lacks synchronization when stopping and restarting the DMA ring. The function performs three critical operations without holding a lock: (1) writes RING_CTRL_ABORT to RING_CONTROL register (line 544), (2) waits for completion (line 545), and (3) writes RING_CTRL_ENABLE to RING_CONTROL register (line 577). If multiple timeout handlers invoke this function concurrently on the same ring, their ring control operations can interleave, causing corrupted ring state. While `hci_dma_queue_xfer()` uses `spin_lock_irq(&rh->lock)` to protect RING_OPERATION1 updates (lines 515-520), and `hci_dma_xfer_done()` uses `spin_lock(&rh->lock)` for RING_OPERATION1 updates (lines 603-609), the `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function does not acquire `rh->lock` during its ring control operations. The spinlock `rh->lock` is initialized at line 308 but never used in `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()`, leaving the abort/restart sequence unprotected against concurrent access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function (lines 533-577) lacks synchronization when stopping and restarting the DMA ring. The function performs three critical operations without holding a lock: (1) writes RING_CTRL_ABORT to RING_CONTROL register (line 536), (2) waits for completion (line 537), and (3) writes RING_CTRL_ENABLE to restart the ring (line 573). While `hci_dma_queue_xfer()` uses `spin_lock_irq(&rh->lock)` to protect RING_OPERATION1 updates (lines 515-521), and `hci_dma_xfer_done()` uses `spin_lock(&rh->lock)` for similar protection (lines 607-613), the `hci_dma_dequeue_xfer()` function never acquires `rh->lock`. This allows concurrent invocations from multiple timeout handlers to interleave ring control operations (abort/enable sequences), corrupting the ring state. The vulnerability exists because the function modifies shared hardware ring control state without synchronization, while other functions in the same file properly use the spinlock for similar operations.
